intro.title: Preserving Memory Through Data
intro.paragraph1: This project builds upon Dr. Christoph Kreutzmüller's groundbreaking research documented in 'Final Sale: The Destruction of Jewish Commercial Activity in Nazi Germany' (2015). His decade-long work with the Leo Baeck Institute created an unprecedented archive of Jewish businesses across Germany.
intro.paragraph2: Our interactive map transforms this scholarly database into an accessible digital experience, documenting Jewish-owned businesses in Berlin from 1900 to 1945. Each marker represents a family enterprise - from corner shops to department stores - that formed the economic fabric of the city.
intro.paragraph3: Navigate through time to explore how these businesses thrived, struggled, and ultimately faced forced closure. By combining historical research with modern visualization, we aim to make this important history accessible to new generations.

kreutzmuller.title: Dr. Christoph Kreutzmüller's Pioneering Work
kreutzmuller.description: This project builds directly upon Dr. Kreutzmüller's groundbreaking 2015 study 'Final Sale: The Destruction of Jewish Commercial Activity in Nazi Germany.' His team spent over a decade meticulously documenting the systematic destruction of Jewish businesses across Germany.
kreutzmuller.methodology: Working with the Leo Baeck Institute, Dr. Kreutzmüller and his researchers analyzed thousands of archival documents, municipal records, trade directories, and survivor testimonies to create an unprecedented database of Jewish commercial life before and during the Nazi period.

database.title: The Leo Baeck Institute Database
database.description: The comprehensive database housed at the Leo Baeck Institute contains detailed records of thousands of Jewish businesses, including registration documents, 'Aryanization' records, forced sales documentation, and personal testimonies from business owners and their families.
database.scope: This invaluable scholarly resource documents not just the businesses themselves, but the human stories behind them - families displaced, livelihoods destroyed, and communities forever changed.

transformation.title: From Archive to Accessibility
transformation.description: StoryTimeMaps transforms this scholarly database into an interactive digital experience, making Dr. Kreutzmüller's research accessible to students, educators, and the general public while maintaining historical accuracy and academic rigor.

plaques.title: Memorial Plaques Initiative
plaques.description: Inspired by the Stolpersteine (stumbling stones) project, we envision installing memorial plaques at the original locations of documented Jewish businesses throughout Berlin.
plaques.vision: These plaques would serve as permanent reminders of the vibrant Jewish commercial life that once flourished in these neighborhoods, connecting digital documentation with physical remembrance.

stolpersteine.title: Inspired by Stolpersteine
stolpersteine.description: Like Gunter Demnig's powerful Stolpersteine project, which commemorates individuals, our memorial plaques would honor the commercial spaces where Jewish families built their livelihoods and served their communities.

future.ctaTitle: Help Bring These Memorials to Life
future.ctaDescription: We're seeking partnerships with Berlin's cultural institutions, educational organizations, and community groups to make memorial plaques a reality. This initiative requires collaboration with city planning, historical preservation, and Jewish community organizations.

community.title: Community Engagement
community.description: We're working with local communities, schools, and Berlin's Jewish organizations to develop educational programs that connect this historical data with contemporary discussions about memory, commerce, and community.

expansion.title: Geographic Expansion
expansion.description: Future phases will extend beyond Berlin to document Jewish businesses in other German cities, creating a comprehensive national picture of economic persecution and loss.

hero.title: Memorial Plaques Initiative
hero.subtitle: Bringing digital memory into the physical streets of Berlin
hero.compactDescription: Help us install memorial plaques at the original locations of Jewish businesses throughout Berlin - connecting digital documentation with physical remembrance.
hero.visionDescription: We envision a Berlin where the memory of Jewish commercial life is preserved not just digitally, but in the very streets where these businesses once thrived. Each plaque will tell the story of a family enterprise, connecting passersby to the rich history that was violently erased.

howItWorks.title: How Memorial Plaques Work
howItWorks.subtitle: Connecting physical memorials with digital storytelling
howItWorks.step1Description: Each plaque is based on verified historical research from the Leo Baeck Institute database, documenting the business name, owner, location, and operational dates.
howItWorks.step2Description: Plaques would be installed at or near the original business locations, serving as permanent street-level memorials visible to all passersby.
howItWorks.step3Description: QR codes on each plaque link to our interactive map, providing visitors with photographs, detailed histories, and the full story of each business.

partners.title: Seeking Partners
partners.description: This initiative requires collaboration across multiple sectors. We are actively seeking partners to help bring memorial plaques to Berlin's streets.
